azerbaijan-caspian.label: Azerbaijan (Caspian)
azerbaijan-caspian.brief: Azerbaijan's water life runs along the Absheron peninsula around its capital. Baku faces the Caspian from a curved bay on the peninsula's southern shore, while the country's newest leisure coast -- Sea Breeze, Nardaran, Bilgah -- lines the northern shore a short sea-distance away but a long, congested road drive around the headland. The Caspian is a closed sea, so every route here is domestic: capital-to-resort hops across the peninsula tip, and a southern run to the relocated Port of Baku at Alat. A fast water shuttle turns a 60-90 minute peninsula drive into a 20-minute crossing and gives the fast-growing north-coast resort belt a direct link to the city.
azerbaijan-caspian.corridor_shape: Absheron peninsula hub-and-spoke: Baku Boulevard (south) rounds the eastern tip to the Sea Breeze / Bilgah resort coast (north); a southern spoke to the Alat port.

kazakhstan-caspian.label: Kazakhstan (Caspian)
kazakhstan-caspian.brief: Aktau is Kazakhstan's only significant seaport city, set on the cliff coast of the arid Mangystau region and the western gateway of the trans-Caspian Middle Corridor. Its cliff-top seaside promenade, seaport and the deep-water ferry terminal at Kuryk ~40 nm south define a coast where all movement is road-bound today. A coastal water route links the Aktau waterfront to the Kuryk port and to the seafront resorts, replacing an exposed desert-highway drive with a direct Caspian crossing and giving the Middle Corridor a passenger-grade first/last leg.
kazakhstan-caspian.corridor_shape: Mangystau coastal spine: Aktau seaport / promenade <-> Kuryk port to the south, plus short intra-Aktau waterfront hops.

baku-azerbaijan.name: Baku
baku-azerbaijan.brief: Baku wraps around a south-facing bay on the Absheron peninsula, its Seaside Boulevard already running daily excursion boats on the Caspian. The city's leisure growth, though, is on the far northern shore of the peninsula -- the master-planned Sea Breeze resort city, the White Beach and Amburan clubs, and the Bilgah beach hotels -- reachable today only by a long road loop around the headland. Rounding the Absheron tip by water collapses that trip and connects the capital directly to its new coast, with a southern link to the relocated Port of Baku at Alat.

aktau-kazakhstan.name: Aktau
aktau-kazakhstan.brief: Aktau is a planned Soviet-era city with no street names, laid out above a dramatic Caspian cliff coast. Its 1.5 km Skalnaya Tropa seaside promenade, the city seaport (already running short yacht cruises), and seafront hotels like the Caspian Riviera front a sea that today carries only cargo and ferries. A passenger water route ties the waterfront to the Kuryk ferry port to the south and gives Mangystau's oil-and-tourism economy its first fast coastal link.

kuryk-kazakhstan.name: Kuryk
kuryk-kazakhstan.brief: Kuryk is Kazakhstan's deep-water Caspian ferry and RoRo port, ~40 nm south of Aktau and a key Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor gateway. Landside it is remote desert; by water it is a direct coastal run from the Aktau waterfront, making a passenger shuttle the natural way to connect the port to the region's only city.
